title: Regions and Geography
subtitle: The backbone of the Atlas: the six regions, Port, the Spine and the Underpass, the border towns between them, and who trades what with whom.
intro: One column per region, plus Port, the Spine and Underpass, the border towns, and the world as a whole. Neighbours sit side by side where the wiki settles the border. Each card lists what it connects to; click a card to draw its lines and read the wiki sentence behind each one. Dashed chips are borders the wiki calls likely or working; dotted are possible. Inferred trade is hidden until you tick the box. Later parts (culture, food, power, history, people, story) add their own headings under each column, so the board grows downward.
schematic: **A board, not a map.** The wiki says the exact map isn't locked ([Geography and Connections](../../wiki/Geography-and-Connections.md)), so the interactive view sorts things into one column per region instead of placing them. Columns are ordered so regions with a settled border sit next to each other (Northwind, Highridge, Deepwood, Ironcrest, Greenvale, Sunplains); nothing else about position means anything. A real map can be drawn from the same data once the geography is locked.
about: Atlas Part 1: the backbone. Regions, the Spine and Underpass, Port, border towns, borders, routes and trade dependencies. Source: the wiki only. Every thing carries its owner page and status; every connection carries its basis (stated or inferred), a certainty where the wiki gives one, and the sentence that supports it. Laid out as a board of region columns, since the wiki says the exact map is not locked. Rebuild with: python3 atlas/tools/atlas_part.py atlas/regions/regions.json

nodes.label: Western Continent
nodes.text: One of three broad landmasses. The wiki does not say which regions sit on it; Ironcrest is described as 'western upland country'.

nodes.label: Northern Continent
nodes.text: One of three broad landmasses. Northwind 'occupies much of the Northern Continent and associated coasts and islands'.

nodes.label: Eastern Continent
nodes.text: One of three broad landmasses. The wiki does not say which regions sit on it; Sunplains is 'southern/eastern country'.

nodes.label: Northwind
nodes.text: Cold northern coasts, islands, sheltered inland valleys and old clan territories. Settlements cluster at harbors, bays, rivers, fisheries and routes south.

facts.Terrain: cold seas, seasonal storms, rocky coasts, sheltered coves, some partially freezing waters, inland routes toward Highridge
facts.Exports: fish, salt and preserved foods, furs and animal products, ships and maritime capacity
facts.Imports: grain, metal goods, medicines, warmer-climate produce
facts.Trade role: Leverage, not an automatic shipping monopoly: its shipbuilding, sailors, ports and knowledge of difficult northern waters make it unusually important to some routes, so storms, fishery disputes, convoy policy or piracy can propagate beyond Northwind without every coastal shipment belonging to it.
facts.Pressures: shifting fish stocks, rising piracy, convoy agreements with Port, accusations that clans cooperate with raiders
facts.Seasons: In winter, northern routes become unreliable.

nodes.short_text: Cold coasts, islands and clan valleys; harbors and fisheries.

nodes.label: Ironcrest
nodes.text: Much of the western upland country: mineral-rich hills, stream valleys, wooded slopes, pasture and farmland around old mining and metalworking centers.

facts.Terrain: mineral hills, stream valleys, wooded slopes, pasture; eastern and southeastern edges grade into Greenvale, Highridge and parts of Deepwood
facts.Exports: ores, metalwork, tools, weapons, industrial craft capacity
facts.Imports: substantial food in industrial districts, timber and fuel, seasonal labor, some luxuries
facts.Trade role: One side of one of the strongest recurring dependency pairs, Ironcrest ↔ Greenvale: industrial settlements buy food, timber, animals and labor; Greenvale farms and workshops buy Ironcrest tools, hardware and metal goods. Price movements on either side can become political disputes. "A long marriage of necessity: useful, intimate and periodically resentful."
facts.Pressures: labor unrest, covert metal shipments, pressure to expand Underpass access, fears of weapon stockpiling
facts.Seasons: Nothing specific to this region. The wiki gives only a general pattern: passes reopen unevenly in spring, heat and water pressure rise in warmer regions in summer, harvest and storms collide in autumn, and northern routes become unreliable in winter.

nodes.short_text: Western uplands: mines, streams, pasture and forges.

nodes.label: Greenvale
nodes.text: The largest major agricultural heartland: broad temperate lowlands with comparatively reliable rainfall and productive soils, market towns, rivers, orchards, wetlands, mills and estates.

facts.Terrain: temperate lowlands and rolling country; grades into Ironcrest foothills, Highridge routes, Deepwood margins and warmer Sunplains country
facts.Exports: grain, produce, livestock products, textiles and other agricultural goods
facts.Imports: metal tools, preservation salt, shipping and caravan access
facts.Trade role: One side of one of the strongest recurring dependency pairs, Ironcrest ↔ Greenvale: Greenvale farms and workshops buy Ironcrest tools, hardware and metal goods, and Ironcrest's industrial settlements buy its food, timber, animals and labor. Border communities can contain mixed families, shared workshops and competing memories. "A long marriage of necessity: useful, intimate and periodically resentful."
facts.Pressures: an unusually abundant harvest or new high-yield seed strain, collapsing prices, land consolidation, co-ops against estates
facts.Seasons: Nothing specific to this region. The wiki gives only a general pattern: passes reopen unevenly in spring, heat and water pressure rise in warmer regions in summer, harvest and storms collide in autumn, and northern routes become unreliable in winter.

nodes.short_text: The largest farming heartland: broad temperate lowlands.

nodes.label: Highridge Plateau
nodes.text: A highland crossroads: routes that avoid or cross parts of the Spine converge here. Exposed uplands, sheltered valleys, steep passes and towns at water and route junctions.

facts.Terrain: exposed uplands, sheltered valleys, steep passes, seasonal streams, grazing country, caravan corridors
facts.Exports: route access, caravan services, brokerage, arbitration, credit, records and specialist knowledge
facts.Trade role: Intermediary: its route position supports tolls, banking, arbitration, caravan services and information exchange. Its leverage comes from making movement easier or harder, not from "producing nothing"; it still has farms, herds, workshops and ordinary local production.
facts.Pressures: caravan attacks, manipulated route closures, accusations of corrupt militia or toll officials, contested infrastructure
facts.Seasons: Nothing specific to this region. The wiki gives only a general pattern: passes reopen unevenly in spring, heat and water pressure rise in warmer regions in summer, harvest and storms collide in autumn, and northern routes become unreliable in winter.

nodes.short_text: Highland crossroads where routes around the Spine meet.

nodes.label: Deepwood
nodes.text: A major forest region: old-growth and managed woodland, river valleys, wetlands, clearings, forest-edge towns, timber districts and restricted areas.

facts.Terrain: old-growth and managed forest, river valleys, wetlands, clearings; routes into foothills and possibly Underpass entrances
facts.Exports: timber, herbs and medicinals, dyes, forest products, specialist ecological knowledge
facts.Imports: selected metal tools, salt, grain and urban goods
facts.Trade role: Controlled extraction: it can matter disproportionately because some forest products are hard to replace quickly. Export restrictions may be ecological, religious, political, local or commercial, and other regions may misread those motives. Bargaining friction, not a single-minded "resource faction".
facts.Pressures: logging beyond accepted limits, fungal disease, isolationists against reformers, hidden-route crime
facts.Seasons: Nothing specific to this region. The wiki gives only a general pattern: passes reopen unevenly in spring, heat and water pressure rise in warmer regions in summer, harvest and storms collide in autumn, and northern routes become unreliable in winter.

nodes.short_text: Old-growth and managed forest, rivers and wetlands.

nodes.label: Sunplains
nodes.text: Warmer, drier southern and eastern country of city-states, irrigated basins, orchard belts, grazing country and coast. Water law is politically important.

facts.Terrain: dry plains, river valleys, irrigated basins, orchard belts, grazing country, coast, scrub, some fertile deltas
facts.Exports: orchard and irrigated crops, oils and wines where appropriate, craft and luxury goods, southern maritime access
facts.Imports: selected timber, metal, furs and northern goods
facts.Trade role: A competitive market: city-states can concentrate wealth, patronage and demand for imported goods while competing fiercely with one another over water, ports, prestige and trade. There's no single Sunplains market actor.
facts.Pressures: drought fears, private control of canals, city-state blocs forming and breaking
facts.Seasons: Nothing specific to this region. The wiki gives only a general pattern: passes reopen unevenly in spring, heat and water pressure rise in warmer regions in summer, harvest and storms collide in autumn, and northern routes become unreliable in winter.

nodes.short_text: Warm, dry south and east: city-states, orchards, irrigation.

nodes.label: Port
nodes.text: The major neutral commercial city. It matters for its network position and institutions, not as the only harbor. Its exact site isn't fixed; it belongs to no kingdom.

facts.Exports: shipping access, repair, warehousing, processing, finance, arbitration, information, neutral exchange
facts.Why it stays central: network effects: agents, credit, warehouses, courts and translators are already there
facts.Position: not fixed; its site should give 'a position convenient to both northern and southern sea routes' and 'access to inland rivers or roads'
facts.Territory: unsettled: Frostbay Way is described 'if Port is territorially separate'
facts.Trade role: Network hub: its dependence on inflows is real but not helplessness. Its power comes from accumulated institutions and network effects (ships, warehouses, credit, repair, translators, courts, guilds and information all meet there), so a disruption in Port can become a continental event even when the original problem is local.

nodes.label: The Spine
nodes.text: The central mountain system the world's geography and transport are organized around. Passes, saddles, inhabited valleys, mining districts, old fortifications and hidden routes. Geologically active.

facts.Physical role: High enough to redirect weather; difficult enough to concentrate travel into passes; geologically active enough for earthquakes and collapses to matter; old and complex enough to hold caves, faults, mineral belts, valleys and isolated communities. It should not be one continuous impassable wall; it contains high peaks, lower saddles, inhabited valleys, pilgrimage routes, mining districts, seasonal passes, old fortifications, hidden routes.
facts.Human role: The range creates political choke points: a pass can matter more than a hundred miles of open border. It explains Highridge's importance, Underpass development, ancient toll states, strategic fortresses, migration corridors, bandit economies and religious pilgrimage traditions.
facts.Seasons: in spring, roads and passes reopen unevenly (Trade and Dependencies)
facts.Touches: Highridge is the only region the wiki ties to it by name

nodes.short_text: The central mountain system everything routes around.

nodes.label: The Underpass
nodes.text: Caves, fault passages, tunnels, settlements and trade routes beneath parts of the Spine. Not one road, not wholly mapped; authority is fragmented.

facts.Functional adjacency: two places not close on the surface may trade intensely because a reliable tunnel branch connects them
facts.Claims: surface kingdoms claim some entrances and sections but rarely control the entire network

gaps: No named cities inside any of the six regions. Port and the border towns are the only named settlements; every region page describes 'cities' only in general.
Only one region is placed on a continent (Northwind, Northern Continent). Which regions sit on the Western and Eastern Continents is not stated.

Port's site and territory are not fixed. The wiki lists conditions its site should meet (convenient to northern and southern sea routes, access to inland rivers or roads) and describes Frostbay Way 'if Port is territorially separate'.

Five region borders aren't established: Ironcrest–Highridge (likely), Greenvale–Highridge (likely), Deepwood–Sunplains (likely), Highridge–Sunplains (possible), and Greenvale–Deepwood (treated as a direct border unless the map contradicts it). Deepwood–Ironcrest is established as a relationship but only as a 'direct or near-direct' frontier.
The region pages and Geography and Connections disagree on certainty: the Greenvale and Ironcrest pages state their Highridge borders plainly, while Geography and Connections calls them likely.
Five region pairs have no border town: Ironcrest–Highridge, Greenvale–Deepwood, Deepwood–Sunplains, Greenvale–Highridge and Highridge–Sunplains.
The wiki doesn't say which regions the Spine touches (only Highridge is tied to it) or which kingdoms hold Underpass entrances.

No rivers, passes or Underpass entrances are named (history mentions provisional 'Ridge Pass Toll Wars'). Geography and Connections lists what the finished map should show: rivers, passes, Underpass entrances, caravan roads, seasonal closures, sea routes, old roads, pilgrimage paths, smuggling corridors.
Directions are thin: Ironcrest west, Northwind north, Sunplains south and east, and Greenvale as 'the eastern agricultural interior' (from Highridge's point of view).
Border Towns and World Overview carry no status label; the Border Towns page calls its six towns 'established working examples'.
Seven names sit in the border-town name bank, unplaced.
